Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like mid-2020, after the COVID shock. The unemployment rate of 11.1% matches June 2020 (the May figure was 13.3% and July's was 10.2%). The 3-month average payroll change of -4.4 million fits April-June 2020 data, though the May and June readings were positive.

The payroll average may be off. For the three months ending June 2020, the changes were roughly -20.7m, +2.7m and +4.8m, which averages about -4.4m. That matches.

The 3-month CPI change and the 12-month YoY readings also fit June 2020: headline CPI was 0.6% and core 1.2%. The fed funds rate was 0.10 and the 10-year yield was 0.55-0.65. Gold's 12-month return of 35.9% fits June 2020, and the VIX near 24.76 fits the end of June, when it was about 30. By the end of July, 2020 the VIX was about 24 and the 10-year yield was about 0.53, which would fit July better. Headline CPI for July was 1.0%, though, which is a mismatch. Unemployment of 11.1% is the June figure, and July's was 10.2%. Publication timing may explain this, since the July jobs report came out in early August.

Gold's 1-month return of 11.3% suggests July 2020, when gold rose about 10%. In June it rose only about 3%. So the snapshot may be end of July, with the latest published unemployment (June, 11.1%) and the CPI for June (0.65%). That fits: June CPI was 0.6%, and 0.71 may be unrounded. The 1-month equity return of 5.2% fits July (S&P rose 5.6%). So the month is July 2020.
